findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced this morning." followed by a list containing only "Beta Launch Plan", "Holiday Campaign Assets", and "Partner Integration Pilot" (3 items)
findings.fix: Either add the fourth project to the list or change the summary text to say "3 projects."
findings.location: workspace-overview section, "Your projects" list beneath the summary paragraph
findings.violation: The stated project count (4) does not match the number of projects actually listed (3), which reads as a data bug to anyone reviewing the mockup.

findings.fix: Add visible label text such as "Duplicate" inside the button, or an icon plus adjacent text, in addition to the aria-label.
findings.violation: The button has no visible text or icon content, only an aria-label, so sighted users see an empty, unlabeled control and have no way to know what it does or that it is even present.

findings.fix: Style the destructive action distinctly, for example a warning color or button treatment, and make Cancel the visually primary choice.
findings.violation: The destructive, team-wide "Archive" action is marked up identically to the safe "Cancel" action, with no visual or semantic distinction, making it easy to trigger by mistake.

findings.evidence: "An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted."
findings.fix: Display the actual email address that was invited in the confirmation message, for example "An invite was sent to {email}."
findings.violation: The confirmation message refers to "the address entered above," but this screen does not display or carry forward the email address that was entered on the previous screen, so the reference has nothing for the reader to look at.

findings.evidence: "Import failed. Error code IMP-500. Contact support if this continues."
findings.fix: Add a retry action and a way to contact support such as a link or button, and consider hiding the raw error code behind a details disclosure rather than showing it by default.
findings.violation: The error message surfaces a raw internal error code to the end user and tells them to "contact support" without providing any way to do so, and gives no option to retry the import.

findings.fix: Mark the user's current setting as the selected option by default by adding the selected attribute to the appropriate option.
findings.violation: Neither option is marked as selected, so a user arriving at this screen cannot tell what their current digest setting is before changing it.

findings.fix: Change the link text or add a status indicator to signal the failed state, for example "Import failed, view details."
findings.location: workspace-overview section, "View last import result" link
findings.violation: This is the only entry point to the import-status screen, but its label gives no indication that the last import failed, so a user has no reason to click it and may never learn about the failure.

findings.evidence: "Archiving \"Vendor Onboarding\" will remove it from the active projects list for everyone on the team."
findings.fix: Require a stronger confirmation step, such as typing the project name or a checkbox acknowledgment, before the archive action becomes available.
findings.violation: A single click on "Archive" immediately performs a team wide, irreversible sounding action with no secondary confirmation such as typing the project name, which is inconsistent with the stated impact.

findings.evidence: <head> contains only <meta charset="utf-8"> and <title>; no <style> or <link rel="stylesheet"> element appears anywhere in the file
findings.fix: Add at minimum basic styling to differentiate buttons, primary actions, and destructive actions from plain links and body text.
findings.violation: With no styling at all, every link and button renders as plain default browser text, so there is no visual hierarchy distinguishing primary actions, destructive actions, or navigation from body text, undermining the document's stated purpose as a mockup.
